what.heading: What is pandas?
paragraphs: **Pandas** is a Python library for working with tables. It holds a table as a **DataFrame**: rows and columns, like a sheet in Excel, that you change with code instead of by hand.
Real tables are messy. A value is missing, a row was entered twice, a number was saved as text. Pandas finds and fixes each of these in one line.

points.title: DataFrame
points.text: The whole table. It's usually called `df`.

points.title: Column
points.text: `df["pages"]` gives one column, called a Series.

points.title: Write it back
points.text: Most cleaning steps give back a new table. Save it with `df = ...`, or `df` stays the same.

what.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv("/content/documents.csv")

example.heading: What it looks like
example.code:
import pandas as pd

docs = [
    {"doc_type": "Certificate of Quality", "lot_number": "AB-4417", "pages": "3"},
    {"doc_type": "Cover Letter", "lot_number": None, "pages": "1"},
    {"doc_type": "Certificate of Quality", "lot_number": "AB-4417", "pages": "3"},
]
df = pd.DataFrame(docs)
print(df)
example.caption: Three problems in three rows: the Cover Letter has no lot number (pandas shows None), the first row appears twice, and the page counts are text in quotes, not numbers. These records are made up.

demos.label: Inspect the table
demos.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame([
    {"doc_type": "Certificate of Quality", "lot_number": "AB-4417", "pages": "3"},
    {"doc_type": "Cover Letter", "lot_number": None, "pages": "1"},
    {"doc_type": "Certificate of Quality", "lot_number": "AB-4417", "pages": "3"},
])
print(df.shape)
df.info()
demos.note: df.shape gives (rows, columns). df.info() lists each column, how many values are filled in (Non-Null Count) and its type (Dtype). lot_number has 2 of 3 filled in, and pages is object, which means text.

demos.label: Count and fill missing values
demos.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame([
    {"doc_type": "Certificate of Quality", "lot_number": "AB-4417"},
    {"doc_type": "Cover Letter", "lot_number": None},
])
print(df.isnull().sum())
df["lot_number"] = df["lot_number"].fillna("unknown")
print(df)
demos.note: isnull().sum() counts the missing values in each column. fillna() fills them. df.dropna() would remove the whole row instead, and you'd lose the Cover Letter.

demos.label: Remove duplicate rows
demos.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame([
    {"doc_type": "Certificate of Quality", "lot_number": "AB-4417"},
    {"doc_type": "Chain of Custody", "lot_number": "CF-2290"},
    {"doc_type": "Certificate of Quality", "lot_number": "AB-4417"},
])
print(df.duplicated().sum())
df = df.drop_duplicates()
print(df)
demos.note: duplicated().sum() counts rows that repeat an earlier row. drop_duplicates() keeps the first copy and removes the rest.

demos.label: Fix a column's type
demos.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"pages": ["3", "1", "2"]})
print(df["pages"].dtype)
print(df["pages"].sum())

df["pages"] = df["pages"].astype(int)
print(df["pages"].sum())
demos.note: The type is object, which means text. Adding up text glues it together, so the first sum prints 312. astype(int) turns each value into a whole number, and the sum becomes 6.

demos.label: Save the clean table
demos.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame([
    {"doc_type": "Certificate of Quality", "pages": 3},
    {"doc_type": "Cover Letter", "pages": 1},
])
df.to_csv("documents_clean.csv", index=False)
print(open("documents_clean.csv").read())
demos.note: to_csv() writes the table to a CSV file, one line per row with commas between values. index=False leaves out the row numbers. In Colab, the file appears in the Files panel.

try.prompt: Clean `df` in three steps: remove the duplicate row, fill the missing `lot_number` with "unknown", and turn `pages` into whole numbers.

try.solution:
import pandas as pd

docs = [
    {"doc_type": "Certificate of Quality", "vendor": "Example Bio Supplies", "lot_number": "AB-4417", "pages": "3"},
    {"doc_type": "Cover Letter", "vendor": "Sample Vials Co.", "lot_number": None, "pages": "1"},
    {"doc_type": "Chain of Custody", "vendor": "Demo Filters Ltd.", "lot_number": "CF-2290", "pages": "2"},
    {"doc_type": "Certificate of Quality", "vendor": "Example Bio Supplies", "lot_number": "AB-4417", "pages": "3"},
]
df = pd.DataFrame(docs)

df = df.drop_duplicates()
df["lot_number"] = df["lot_number"].fillna("unknown")
df["pages"] = df["pages"].astype(int)

print(df)

checks.hint: Keep the table in a variable named df. Start from the starter code, which builds df with pd.DataFrame(docs).
The Cover Letter row is gone. dropna() removes every row with a missing value. Use fillna("unknown") on the lot_number column instead, so the row stays.
df still has the repeated Certificate of Quality row. Write df = df.drop_duplicates(). On its own, drop_duplicates() gives back a new table and leaves df as it was.
df should have 3 rows: the Certificate of Quality, the Cover Letter and the Chain of Custody.
lot_number still has a missing value. Write the filled column back: df["lot_number"] = df["lot_number"].fillna("unknown").
Fill the missing lot_number with the text "unknown", in lowercase and in quotes.
pages should hold whole numbers, not text or decimals. Write df["pages"] = df["pages"].astype(int).
